newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures closes higher after modest recovery.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures closes higher after modest recovery.

text.p: FCOJ futures settled higher as the market looked to be recovering slightly from recent steep selloffs while traders awaited Thursday's USDA Florida crop report amid a background of cooler weather in Florida.
"The market has been oversold," PaineWebber analyst Bernard Savaiko said. "The USDA crop report might be making some bears nervous and there is also talk about cold weather."
These two factors lent some support for the nearby January spot month which closed 1.90 cents higher at 78.30 cents per pound, Savaiko added.
Most-active March saw more modest gains, ending 1.20 cents firmer at 81.60 cents per pound, traded 82.50 to 81.40 cents.
Volume was estimated at 3,500 lots, up from Friday's official 1,444 lots.

Weatherman Jon Davis of Smith Barney said the coldest air is not expected to flow directly into the Florida peninsula, where temperatures were set to be cooler but not low enough to damage any unharvested crop.
"Keep in mind that the majority of the fruit has already been harvested," Davis said.
